semantics.note: 'I do genuinely think... will' is a firm expectation, not a hedge. The 'long term' qualifier comes from the source, and the context adds 'eventually (no time soon)'. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Reading 'all' as most people and 'armies' as large fleets is an ordinary plain reading. With no deadline, the contract correctly allows only early support or a decisive collapse.

evidence.note: Salesforce's own disclosure of Agentforce deal growth in late 2025. This is growing enterprise use, far short of near-universal personal agents. It does not meet the early-resolution rule.

reviews.rationale: This is a long-term forecast with no deadline. The packet does not show most people using personal agents or companies routinely running fleets of them, so early support is not met. There is no decisive collapse either. It stays open.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'All that we will have this year are demos' is a firm, unhedged forecast for 2025. The normalised proposition matches it.

contract.note: The plain reading (only demos, no real production or paid agent products in 2025) is the ordinary sense of an unqualified 'all'. The 'narrow use cases' exception attaches to the previous sentence about doing a huge share of work, and the contract flags it. I judge the reading fair.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure: Claude Code was generally available from May 2025 and used by large enterprises. That is a product, not a demo.
Anthropic's own disclosure of a $1B run rate by November 2025, which shows paid use at scale. It is a run rate, used only as evidence of real use.
Salesforce earnings release: over 9,500 paid Agentforce deals and growing production accounts by October 2025.
Shows general agents were still unreliable in 2025. That backs his reliability point, not the 'only demos' claim.

reviews.rationale: The 2025 horizon has passed. Under the fair plain reading, agent products were generally available, used in production and paid for at scale in 2025. Coding agents and Agentforce went well beyond demos. The support condition (no significant production use or paying customers) failed.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A necessity claim: reliable agents require solving hallucination. The second clause is split into a separate claim. This is fine.

contract.note: 'Reliable' and 'solve' are undefined, so the result turns on thresholds the speaker did not give. The refutation condition is a fair one, but the claim can only fail to be refuted, never be confirmed directly.

evidence.note: OpenAI paper says hallucinations persist. That bears on the second clause, not on whether reliable agents need it solved first.
A single agent failure that involved false statements. It is consistent with the claim but cannot show hallucination is a necessary barrier.

reviews.rationale: No evidence isolates whether hallucination is a necessary barrier to reliable agents. Nor does any show agents widely accepted as reliable despite hallucinating. With no agreed threshold for 'reliable', the packet neither refutes nor supports the necessity claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'There is still no principled trustworthy answer' describes the field's state at the January 2025 post date. It is correctly treated as an observation.

contract.note: Reading 'principled trustworthy answer' as a method that reliably prevents hallucinations, not one that only reduces or partly detects them, is a fair, ordinary plain reading. January 2025 is a reasonable target period.

evidence.note: Nature feature from 21 January 2025: hallucinations can't be stopped, and techniques only limit the damage.
OpenAI's own system card for o3-mini (end of January 2025) reports a 14.8% PersonQA hallucination rate and says more work is needed. This is a company disclosure.
Georgia Tech's summary of the Nature feature: researchers were working to make hallucinations less frequent, not eliminate them.
2024 semantic-entropy method detects only a subset of hallucinations and does not prevent them, so it is not a full answer. It falls outside the target period.

reviews.rationale: Sources from January 2025 (Nature, and OpenAI's o3-mini system card) show hallucinations persisted and were only being reduced. The strongest counterpoint detects only a subset. No method reliably eliminating hallucinations existed by January 2025.
